h: פָּרָשַׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ, מַאֲמָר ח׳ Parshas HaChodesh — Maamar Ches

p: "And on the Shabbos day it shall be opened,
and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened."
why were they not mentioned on the festivals,
Likewise one must examine what is said
"And it shall be, every new moon in its month
and every Shabbos in its Shabbos,
and here too the festivals are not mentioned,
though on them there is the mitzvah of appearing.
וְהִנֵּה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִצְטַוּוּ בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה
Now, that they were not commanded at present
one can say it is because of the burden,
that it should properly have been
But in the future there will be no burden,
as they said in Pesikta Rabbasi
(לְשַׁבָּת וְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ פָּרָשָׁה א סִימָן ג)
(on Shabbos and Rosh Chodesh, parshah 1, siman 3),
and bring them to Yerushalayim, etc.
and when Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbos
But at any rate, on the festivals,
when there is a mitzvah even now
that they will come to bow down?
Surely the Torah will not change!
that in all the festivals there is a holiness
when he comes to the place of the Mikdash,
And this will be opened in the future
that they will be able to sense,
in every place in Eretz Yisrael,
that in every month there is
for so the birth of the moon is called
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה׳.
as it is said: "For Hashem is a sun and a shield."
every Shabbos has a renewed holiness,
it would not be called a bride,
for a bride is a bride only for the seven days.
רַק בְּכָל שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה
Rather, each Shabbos has a new holiness,
as we have said many times.
And about this it is said:
and every Shabbos in its Shabbos" —
and the body is "the flesh of man,"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב עו, א).
And this is from the holiness of
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
דְּאִיתָא (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן יג כט, א)
for it is stated (Tikkunei Zohar, tikkun 13, 29a)
since they are all his offspring.
And this holiness they will receive anew
and they will go up for the pilgrimage,
yet the main appearance will be
for the sake of the Shabbos within it;
and Shavuos, although it is one day,
has make-up days for all seven
But the holiness that one senses on the festival
in every place in Eretz Yisrael,
for it will be like Yerushalayim.
And this is what is said:
and every Shabbos in its Shabbos
And so regarding the Shunamite it is written:
"It is neither new moon nor Shabbos,"
to greet his teacher on the festival.
and he must greet his teacher then;
"It is an obligation upon a person
to greet the face of the Shechinah
on every new moon and Shabbos;
and who is his teacher," etc.,
so that on a new moon and Shabbos
and he asked why she was going
when it was neither new moon nor Shabbos.
it is written: "On the Shabbos day it shall be opened,
and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened":
for then there will be opened
upon Knesses Yisrael, as was said.
And when Shabbos and the new moon join together,
the holiness of both Shabbos and the new moon.

paragraphs.text: Ezekiel 46:1 — “Thus says the Lord Hashem: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be closed during the six working days, but on the Shabbos day it shall open, and on the day of the new moon it shall open.” The verse names Shabbos and the new moon as the times of opening. Rav Tzadok asks why the festivals, discussed in the preceding prophecy, are not also named here.

paragraphs.text: Isaiah 66:23 — “It shall be, from new moon to new moon, and from Shabbos to Shabbos, that all flesh shall come to bow before Me, says Hashem.” The repeated specification of month and Shabbos parallels the opening in Yechezkel. Rav Tzadok reads the renewed sanctity as reaching bodily experience, not only the soul.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Pinchas 15 — “It would have been fitting for the assembly after Sukkos to be fifty days after the festival, just as the assembly after Pesach is fifty days later. But the Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘It is winter, and they cannot leave their homes to come here. Instead, while they are with Me, let them hold the assembly.’” The Midrash explains Shemini Atzeres by the difficulty of returning in winter. Rav Tzadok invokes this as an example of the burden of travel in the present order of things.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbati 1 — “How can all flesh come to Jerusalem every month and every Shabbos? Rabbi Levi said: Jerusalem is destined to be like the Land of Israel, and the Land of Israel like the whole world. How will they come on the new moon and Shabbos from the end of the world? Clouds will come, carry them, and bring them to Jerusalem, and they will pray there in the morning. ... If the new moon falls on Shabbos, Rabbi Pinchas the priest, son of Chama, said in Rabbi Reuven’s name: They come twice, once for Shabbos and once for the new moon. The clouds carry them early and bring them to Jerusalem. ... ‘Who are these who fly like a cloud’—this is the morning; ‘and like doves to their windows’—this is the afternoon.” The checked chapter explicitly supplies both the effortless transport and the double coming. Its internal §3 is the manuscript’s locator; the chapter text is the verified digital witness.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 119a — “Rabbi Chanina would wrap himself and stand toward the evening of Shabbos. He said: ‘Come, let us go out to meet Shabbos the queen.’ Rabbi Yannai dressed in fine garments and said: ‘Come, bride; come, bride.’” The Gemara provides the paired images of queen and bride. Rav Tzadok develops the bridal image as a fresh encounter with sanctity each Shabbos.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 76a, Yisro — “When Adam was created, what is written of him? ‘You clothed me in skin and flesh.’ If so, what is the human being? If you say he is nothing but skin, flesh, bones, and sinews, it is not so, for the human being is certainly nothing but the soul. What are called skin, flesh, bones, and sinews are all only a garment: they are the human being’s clothing, and are not the human being. When that human being departs, he strips off those garments in which he was clothed.” The 76a marker occurs within this paragraph. The distinction between the inward person and bodily clothing underlies Rav Tzadok’s emphasis that “all flesh” itself will receive the renewed holiness.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 4b — “Rabbi Elazar said in Rabbi Oshaya’s name: From where do we know that Shavuos has compensatory days for all seven days? Scripture says, ‘On the festival of matzos, on the festival of Shavuos, and on the festival of Sukkos.’ It compares Shavuos to the festival of matzos: Just as the festival of matzos has compensatory days for all seven days, so Shavuos has compensatory days for all seven days.” This concerns the opportunity to bring the festival offerings after the first day. Rav Tzadok notes that the seven-day period consequently includes a Shabbos even when Shavuos itself falls on a weekday.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 16b — “Rabbi Yitzchak said: A person must receive the presence of his teacher on the festival, as it is said: ‘Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Shabbos.’ This implies that on new moon and Shabbos she ought to go.” The proof is from the question addressed to the Shunammite woman in II Melachim 4:23. Rav Tzadok distinguishes the festival obligation from the additional responsiveness of someone who perceives the renewed holiness of each month and Shabbos.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shoftim 2 — on the Baal HaTurim’s link between “all your males shall appear” and the duty to greet one’s teacher: “The mitzvah of appearing on the three festivals corresponds to the three Avos, that their holiness appear in Yisrael’s heart.” This adds what the festival holiness is. It is the holiness of the Avos coming into the heart, and that is why one goes to his rebbe then.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 265b, Vaeschanan — “Rabbi Abba was coming from seeing Rabbi Shimon when Rabbi Yitzchak encountered him. He said: ‘From where have you come, master of light, a man who cleaves to the fire that consumes every day? Light indeed rests with him.’ He replied: ‘We learned that a person is obligated to receive the presence of the Shechinah on every new moon and Shabbos. Who is this? His teacher. All the more so the supernal holy lamp, whose presence all people of the world seek to receive.’ Rabbi Yitzchak said: ‘I will return with you, receive the presence of the Shechinah, and taste those supernal words that you tasted before him.’” The exact Aramaic is verified in Vaeschanan 16:5. The preceding chapter 15 carries the Hebrew folio marker 265b, and the next chapter 17 carries 266a. The story explicitly joins receiving one’s teacher to tasting Torah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shelach 14 — “In the future the clouds will carry them to Yerushalayim, and then there will be an obligation every month and Shabbos; in this world it is optional, as we find, ‘neither new moon nor Shabbos.’” This draws the halachic line. Going each month and Shabbos is a matter of choice in this world, for one who feels its holiness. In the future it will be required of all.
